title: Crossclaims against a coparty
summary: A crossclaim is a claim against a coparty, such as one defendant’s claim against another defendant. Rule 13(g) requires the specified connection to the transaction, occurrence, or property involved in the action.
notes: A crossclaim is distinct from a counterclaim against an opponent and from impleading someone not yet a party. Jurisdiction remains an additional inquiry.

sections.Meaning: A crossclaim is a claim against a coparty, such as one defendant’s claim against another defendant. Rule 13(g) requires the specified connection to the transaction, occurrence, or property involved in the action.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify why the parties are coparties, what relief is sought, and how the claim relates to the original dispute or a counterclaim. LASA examines connected claims among construction participants.
